findings.reason: a worker implementing §2 as written builds a second policy layer and must silently reconcile it with `RowPolicy` inside `_follow_watch_lines`, or reverts it; the section must instead state whether the new module replaces, extends or wraps the existing policy.
findings.text: §2 proposes a new pure module `reckon/crew/row_policy.py` that "holds a run's change until it has gone a settle window with no further transition", but `reckon/crew/ticker.py` already ships `RowPolicy` (line 1161) with `NOISE_PAIRS` hold windows, `PaneRowPath`, and `replay_row_policy`, and `reckon/cli.py:3723` already builds it via `follower_row_path`, which `_follow_watch_lines` calls at line 4042; the plan names none of these and so describes work that duplicates a landed, tested mechanism (tests/test_follower_prints_only_policy_rows.py)

findings.reason: §4 is largely shipped (commit 1d08e629a "replay the gap a follower missed between armings"); as written it sends a node to re-implement landed behaviour, and the plan should reduce §4 to verifying it and adding any genuinely missing edge.
findings.text: §4's deliverable — "when a follower attaches, it draws no row for a run whose current state equals the state the reader last judged", the first-attach summary line, and withholding the dim history burst under session-host delivery — is already implemented: `_follow_gap_rows` in `reckon/cli.py` drops a run whose `recorded == current`, `delivered_states`/`read_delivered`/`write_delivered` persist the judged state, and `_follow_replay_visible()` (reckon/cli.py:4878) already hands the history burst only to a terminal, not the host's pipe Monitor; the plan cites none of this and asserts the behaviour as an unmet deliverable

findings.reason: a gate that passes on the unfixed code measures nothing new; §4's measure needs a case the current gap-replay does not already satisfy, or the section should be a verify-and-add-test node, not an implement node.
findings.text: §4's done-when asserts a second attach "draws only the completion, and draws no bare `working` row", with a negative control that removes "the judged-state comparison", but the judged-state comparison is `_follow_gap_rows`'s existing `if recorded == current: continue`, so the test passes on the unmodified tree and its negative control merely restates the existing guard

findings.reason: the relationship is genuinely intended but, being advisory rather than a gate, its absence does not misroute a node; adding the metadata tag would make the advisory edge machine-readable.
findings.text: §1 states the active plan `a-follower-keeps-your-work-in-view` "should weigh this plan's measurement before building that cadence", but the plan declares no `informs` relationship to it (declare `informs`→`informs`), so the advisory edge exists only in prose
